minutes.headline: Water commissioners dedicated a room to John Esposito, approved the budget and annual meeting articles, and heard PFAS and development concerns.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with a presentation dedicating the new headquarters conference room to a retiring-minded commissioner for donated site work and equipment. The board approved prior minutes, an engineering proposal for lead service line inventory, the 2023-24 budget and the annual meeting warrant articles. Residents raised PFAS soil contamination from Hickory Hills well flushing and concerns about a proposed district expansion near a contaminated property.

public_comment.topic: Clarified when she speaks for the Woodlands trustees versus personally.
Read a Woodlands trustees letter asking the district to stop discharging Hickory Hills well water onto Woodlands land, test the soil for PFAS, and remediate if elevated.
Concerns about contamination history at the 110 George Street property proposed for district expansion; asked for an open town-wide public discussion before any special meeting.
Asked the timeline for applying for state revolving fund money for the Hickory Hills well.
A resident of Boyle Park asked about pilot-study discharge from the hydrant near the lake and soil testing.
Vice president of the Hickory Hills lake board described volunteer stormwater and water testing with a consultant.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of January 25th and February 8th.
Approve the engineering proposal for lead service line inventory and have the chair sign it.
Approve the 2023-24 maintenance and operating budget.
Approve the articles for the annual meeting warrant.

budget_items.topic: Lead service line inventory engineering proposals
budget_items.what_was_said: Four proposals were received and close in price; the board chose the firm that included grant application support and GIS equipment given to the district.
Money would go on the annual article and be funded through state clean water funding with possible principal forgiveness, which might become a grant.

budget_items.topic: Mass Ave water main replacement revised budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The budget rose from the 2021 figure to a much higher current estimate, including a large contingency, and requires an article to appropriate more.
Total budget rose from last year, driven by maintenance, chemicals, retirement and electric, partly offset by paid-off loans.
Article 5 again takes money from the water enhancement account for main repair; articles 6 and 7 cover the Mass Ave increase and lead inventory.
The superintendent estimated a first phase done in-house, and noted prevailing wage raises job costs on contracted work.
Donated equipment and labor for the new facility were said to have saved the district a very large sum.

budget_items.topic: State revolving fund for Hickory Hills treatment
budget_items.what_was_said: The district plans to apply after a pilot study, with an August deadline, hoping for PFAS-related funding.

transfers.description: Annual article: take from the water enhancement account into repair of water mains and new installation
transfers.outcome: discussed only (warrant approved as a slate)

decisions.decision: The conference room at 496 Massachusetts Avenue was dedicated as the John Esposito room, with a plaque to be placed.
The developer will be on the next meeting's agenda; the board will request DEP paperwork on the site and call a special meeting and public hearing if required.
The superintendent was asked to contact DEP about concerns for supplying water to the proposed area.
The board will consult legal counsel and DEP regarding the Woodlands PFAS request.

what_happened.line: The board approved the 2023-24 maintenance and operating budget by voice vote; the count was not stated.
It approved the annual meeting warrant articles, including a further appropriation for the Mass Ave water main replacement and funding for a lead service line inventory.
It approved an engineering proposal for the lead service line inventory, choosing the firm that included grant application support, and the chair was authorized to sign.
The board will request DEP paperwork on a proposed expansion site and consult legal counsel and DEP on a PFAS soil-testing request from the Woodlands trustees.
The conference room at the new headquarters was dedicated as the John Esposito room, with a plaque to follow.

why_it_matters: The budget and warrant articles approved here are what district voters will be asked to act on at the annual meeting, including more money for the Mass Ave main and the lead pipe inventory.

Residents near Hickory Hills and the Woodlands, and near the proposed expansion site, have raised PFAS and contamination questions that could shape water-treatment costs and where the district extends service.
watch_next: The developer for the proposed expansion is to be on the next meeting's agenda, and a special meeting and public hearing may be called if required.
The district plans to apply for state revolving fund money for Hickory Hills treatment after a pilot study, with an August deadline.
